description: High-throughput memory alignment, zero-copy, lock-free ring buffers, cache locality, and latency optimization.

topics.title: Cache Locality & Data-Oriented Design vs OOP
topics.definition: Data-Oriented Design (DOD) prioritizes the layout of data in hardware memory (L1/L2/L3 caches) to maximize cache hits, contrasting traditional OOP (Array of Structures - AoS) with Structure of Arrays (SoA).
topics.why_it_matters: A cache miss can cost 200+ CPU cycles while an L1 cache hit takes only 4 cycles. High-performance game engines, quant trading, and database engines organize data layout to eliminate pointer indirection cache misses.
topics.real_world_analogy: A grocery warehouse: if order pickers only need product weights, storing weights in one contiguous ledger allows fast scanning of 1,000 items in a single glance (SoA), rather than walking to 1,000 separate aisles to read each full product box (AoS).
conceptual_breakdown: CPU Cache Lines: Memory is loaded in 64-byte chunks. Touching one byte loads the adjacent 63 bytes into L1 cache for free.
Array of Structures (AoS): Classic OOP layout: struct Particle { float x, y, z; int id; string name; }; vector. Iterating over positions wastes cache bandwidth fetching unused names and IDs.
Structure of Arrays (SoA): Data-Oriented layout: struct ParticleSystem { vector x, y, z; };. SIMD auto-vectorization and pure contiguous cache line utilization.
Pointer Chasing Penalty: Classic polymorphic OOP (vector>) scatters objects across the heap, causing L1 cache misses on almost every dereference.

classes.name: ArrayOfStructures_AoS
methods: Low cache locality for position update (wastes bandwidth on names)

steps.description: CPU fetches 64-byte Cache Line from RAM containing 16 contiguous float coordinates (SoA).
SIMD AVX-512 register loads 16 floats in parallel and updates coordinates in 1 cycle.
In contrast, AoS pointer dereference incurs 200ns RAM stall on every object jump.

step_by_step_explanation: 1. 64-Byte Cache Line Saturation: By storing float x[] sequentially, a single 64B cache line fetch delivers 16 sequential coordinates with zero wasted bytes.
2. SIMD Auto-Vectorization: Modern compilers (GCC `-O3`, Clang, MSVC) transform the SoA loop into 512-bit vector registers processing 16 updates per clock.
3. Elimination of Pointer Dereferencing: Contiguous vectors eliminate heap fragmentation and translation lookaside buffer (TLB) thrashing.

common_mistakes.correction: Use DOD data pools or contiguous arrays of concrete types to avoid pointer chasing.

interview_traps:
Trap: 'Should we always rewrite all OOP systems into SoA?'
Answer: No. Apply DOD to hot batch-processing loops (physics, graphics, matching engines, analytics); keep traditional OOP for high-level business entities and complex state machines.

code_refactor_exercise.problem: Refactor a polymorphic game entity update loop into a cache-friendly component data array.
code_refactor_exercise.bad_code: for (auto& entity : entities) entity->update(); // Virtual call + cache miss

practice_problem.title: Design Entity-Component-System (ECS) Storage
practice_problem.description: Implement a sparse-set ECS storage mechanism that maps Entity IDs to contiguous Component arrays in O(1) time.
practice_problem.hint: Use a sparse array `sparse[entityId] = denseIndex` and packed dense array `dense[denseIndex] = component`.

topics.title: Lock-free SPSC Ring Buffer Design
topics.definition: A Single-Producer Single-Consumer (SPSC) circular queue utilizing atomic head/tail indices and memory order fences (Acquire-Release) to achieve wait-free, zero-lock IPC and inter-thread messaging.
topics.why_it_matters: Standard mutex-based queues incur kernel context switches (1-5 microseconds) and priority inversions. SPSC queues deliver nanosecond latency (sub-20ns) essential for high-frequency trading and real-time audio.
topics.real_world_analogy: A conveyor belt sushi bar with 1 chef (Producer) placing dishes on empty rotating plates and 1 customer (Consumer) picking them up without ever stopping or speaking to each other.
conceptual_breakdown: Circular Ring Buffer: Fixed-size array with power-of-two capacity for fast bitwise modulo: index = pos & (capacity - 1).
Atomic Indices: std::atomic head (written only by Consumer) and std::atomic tail (written only by Producer).
Acquire-Release Memory Ordering: Producer uses std::memory_order_release on tail write; Consumer uses std::memory_order_acquire on tail read.
False Sharing Prevention: alignas(hardware_destructive_interference_size) to keep head and tail on separate 64-byte cache lines.

steps.description: Producer checks (tail - head < Capacity). Buffer has free slot.
Producer writes item into buffer[tail & mask] with no locks.
Producer increments tail with memory_order_release. Data is visible to Consumer.
Consumer loads tail with memory_order_acquire, reads item, and advances head.

step_by_step_explanation: 1. False Sharing Elimination: alignas(64) places head and tail into separate cache lines, eliminating core-to-core cache line bouncing.
2. Acquire-Release Semantics: std::memory_order_release on tail publish guarantees all written item bytes in the array are committed before the index increment is observed by the consumer.
3. Bitwise Fast Modulo: Power of 2 constraint allows tail & (Capacity - 1) instead of expensive integer division instructions.

common_mistakes.correction: Causes false sharing, degrading throughput by up to 80% due to cache line invalidation between CPU cores.
Allows CPU out-of-order execution to publish the tail index BEFORE the array data is written, resulting in uninitialized data reads.

interview_traps:
Trap: 'Can this SPSC queue be used safely with 2 Producers and 1 Consumer?'
Answer: Absolutely not. SPSC assumes single-writer per index. Multiple producers require MPMC queues using `atomic::compare_exchange_weak` and sequence numbers (e.g. Dmitry Vyukov's MPMC queue).

code_refactor_exercise.problem: Refactor a mutex-guarded audio playback buffer into a lock-free SPSC ring buffer to prevent audio stutter glitches.
code_refactor_exercise.good_code: spscQueue.push(sample); // Real-time safe, never blocks audio thread

practice_problem.title: Design Batch-Push SPSC Queue
practice_problem.description: Implement `push_batch(const T* data, size_t count)` that writes multiple elements under a single atomic tail update.
practice_problem.hint: Check available capacity once: `(Capacity - (tail - head)) >= count`, write range, then store `tail + count`.

topics.title: Zero-Copy Buffer Abstractions
topics.definition: Designing network and file I/O abstractions (`std::string_view`, `std::span`, scatter-gather I/O) that inspect and slice data without copying bytes across user and kernel memory spaces.
topics.why_it_matters: Copying memory is CPU-intensive. At 100 Gbps network speeds, traditional `std::string` copies will saturate memory bus bandwidth. Zero-copy abstractions enable line-rate network packet processing.
topics.real_world_analogy: Highlighting a sentence in a physical library book and passing the page coordinates (Page 42, Line 10) to a colleague, rather than hand-copying the entire 500-page book onto new sheets of paper.
conceptual_breakdown: std::string_view & std::span (C++20): Non-owning reference views over contiguous memory slices consisting of just a pointer and a size.
Scatter-Gather I/O (vectored I/O): writev and readv allow sending multiple non-contiguous memory buffers in a single system call.
Ring Buffer Slicing: Passing pointer offsets into existing packet receive buffers directly to parsers.
Ownership Boundaries: Ensuring source memory buffer lifetime outlives all referencing views.

steps.description: NIC transfers 1500B Ethernet frame directly into DMA Ring Buffer.
Parser creates zero-copy std::span views for IP Header and TCP Payload without copying.
Application processes payload directly in DMA memory. Latency is minimized.

step_by_step_explanation: 1. std::span Contiguous Memory View: std::span represents any contiguous buffer (vector, raw array, memory-mapped file) without owning or copying it.
2. Subspan Zero-Copy Slicing: rawFrame.subspan() performs an $O(1)$ offset calculation rather than copying bytes into a new container.
3. Reinterpretation of Network Structs: Uses `#pragma pack` and pointer reinterpretation to read binary headers directly from wire buffers.

common_mistakes.mistake: Returning a `std::string_view` to a temporary local `std::string`
common_mistakes.correction: The temporary string is destroyed at the end of the statement, creating a catastrophic dangling pointer.

interview_traps:
Trap: 'What is the danger of `reinterpret_cast` for zero-copy parsing across different CPU architectures?'
Answer: Endianness differences (Big-endian network order vs Little-endian x86) and unaligned memory access faults on ARM architectures. Use `ntohs`/`ntohl` or `std::endian` checks.

code_refactor_exercise.problem: Refactor a function taking `const std::string&` that uses `s.substr()` inside a loop.
code_refactor_exercise.bad_code: void parse(const string& s) { auto sub = s.substr(0, 10); } // Heap copy every slice
code_refactor_exercise.good_code: void parse(string_view s) { auto sub = s.substr(0, 10); } // O(1) pointer slice

practice_problem.title: Design Scatter-Gather Chunk Buffer
practice_problem.description: Implement a `ChunkedBuffer` that chains multiple 4KB zero-copy memory blocks and exposes a unified `read_view(offset, len)` interface.
